title: Apply the Tolerance Policy to the Batch
scenario: It is 10:30 AM. The tolerance policy is owned, versioned config the matching engine applies the same way every time. Read it, then apply it to two invoices with price gaps - one small, one large - and see the band do its job.
input: Price variance allowed within the LARGER of 2% of the PO amount or $25.00. Quantity must match exactly. Approved by the Controller, effective day-0. Batch gaps to test: INV-59002 bills $1,230.00 vs PO $1,140.00 (gap $90.00, PO band = max(2% of 1140 = 22.80, 25) = 25.00). INV-59005 bills $1,000.00 vs PO $992.00 (gap $8.00, PO band = max(2% of 992 = 19.84, 25) = 25.00).
instructions: Read the tolerance policy as owned, versioned config - not an opinion.
Compute each invoice's band as the larger of 2% of the PO and $25.00.
Compare each price gap to its band: INV-59002's $90 is outside, INV-59005's $8 is inside.
Answer the governance questions and validate to mint the policy record.

questions.prompt: What is INV-59002's tolerance band, and does its $90 gap pass?

options.text: Band $25.00 (larger of 2% of 1140 and 25); the $90 gap fails

questions.explain: 2% of the $1,140 PO is $22.80, and the absolute floor is $25.00, so the band is the larger: $25.00. A $90.00 gap is far outside it, so the price leg fails and the invoice is an exception.

questions.prompt: INV-59005's gap is $8.00 against a $25.00 band. What does the policy say about its price?

options.text: It fails - any gap is a failure
It passes - $8 is within the $25 band
It cannot be judged without the receipt

questions.explain: $8.00 sits inside the $25.00 band, so on price alone INV-59005 is within tolerance. (Its problem is a missing receipt, which is a separate leg of the match - not a price issue.)

questions.prompt: Why is the band 'the LARGER of 2% or $25' rather than just 2%?

options.text: So small POs still get a reasonable absolute allowance instead of a tiny percentage

questions.explain: On a small PO, 2% could be just a few dollars and would flag trivial rounding. The $25 floor gives a sensible minimum allowance; the larger-of rule keeps both fair.

questions.prompt: Who may change these tolerance bands, and why does that matter?

options.text: The AP Clerk, to clear stuck invoices faster
The Controller - looser bands move money faster but catch fewer errors, so the change is governed and versioned

questions.explain: Tolerance is a control on how much price error passes automatically. Loosening it is a real risk decision, so only the Controller may approve a change and every version is recorded.

artifactOnPass.rule: larger of 2% of PO or 25.00; quantity exact

copilotPrompt: Apply a tolerance policy (larger of 2% of the PO or $25) to two invoices: compute each band, decide which price gap passes, explain why the rule uses the larger-of form, and who governs changes.
successMessage: Tolerance applied. INV-59002's $90 gap is outside the band; INV-59005's $8 is inside - price-wise.

intro.heading: Before you match: the band is owned config

sections.title: One rule, applied the same way
sections.body: The tolerance policy is versioned config the matching engine reads. Because it is written down and owned, every invoice is judged by the same band - not by whoever is at the desk that day.

sections.title: The larger-of band
sections.body: The allowance is the larger of 2% of the PO or a $25 floor. For these invoices both bands land at $25. INV-59002's $90 gap blows past it; INV-59005's $8 gap sits comfortably inside.

sections.title: Loosening the band is a risk decision
sections.body: A wider band pays faster but lets more price error through. That trade-off is why only the Controller may change the policy, and why every version is recorded - governance before automation.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd write the match tolerances down (e.g. 'price within 2%, quantity exact') in a config tab so the match check uses one agreed rule set.

bestFit.how: Environment Variables or a config list holding the tolerance limits, owned by the Controller
a config dict with a version and an effective date, so an old run can be re-explained
a data store record read at the top of the scenario rather than a number typed into a filter

takeaway.heading: Tolerance policy applied
points: You applied one owned, versioned band consistently to two different price gaps.
INV-59002's $90 gap is outside the $25 band, so its price leg fails and it becomes an exception.
INV-59005's $8 gap is inside the band - its block is a missing receipt, a separate leg, not a price problem.
The larger-of-2%-or-$25 form keeps small POs fair, and only the Controller may change it.
The workflow can now judge every price gap against the same governed tolerance band.
